verifications.note: Colorado Interstate Gas Company's own FY2008 Form 10-K, under 'Projects Placed In Service': 'In November 2008, the High Plains pipeline was placed in service, which is owned by WYCO and operated by us [CIG].' Same 10-K also states the High Plains construction was completed in Q4 2008 and CIG took title/leaseback via a Nov. 1, 2008-effective lease with WYCO.

El Paso Corporation's (CIG's parent, separate SEC registrant/CIK) FY2008 Form 10-K independently states: 'In November 2008, the High Plains pipeline was placed in service,' and separately lists 'Colorado Interstate Gas (CIG)' as a named pipeline system extending from the Rocky Mountain/Anadarko Basin production areas -- matching this row's StartLocation/StartState-Province values -- and its 2008 project-completions summary credits placing 'the High Plains Pipeline in November' among that year's finished expansions.

resolutions.researcher_notes: StartYear1=2008 is corroborated: CIG's own FY2008 10-K and parent El Paso Corp's separately filed FY2008 10-K (different SEC registrants/CIKs, each independently certified) both state the High Plains pipeline -- a 164-mile, WYCO-owned, CIG-operated lateral that is part of the aggregated CIG system this row represents (system spans Rocky Mountains/Anadarko Basin production areas to Colorado/California per StartLocation/EndLocation) -- was placed in service in November 2008. No contradicting date found. Flag for the orchestrator: this 2008 date documents only the High Plains lateral's in-service date, not the CIG mainline's original construction (CIG began service in 1928 per Wikipedia and the Hart Energy 'Rockies Midstream Infrastructure' retrospective, neither of which mentions a 2008 start) -- worth a human check on whether StartYear1 is meant to capture the whole aggregated system's original start or its most recent major addition, since as recorded it reads as if the entire 6,920 km / 5,150 MMcf/d system dates only to 2008.
